text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The constitution of the Sarajevo canton remains one of the most disputed issues between the two ruling parties in Bosnia, the Croat Democratic Union (HDZ) and Moslem Party for Democratic Action (SDA). Talks held in Sarajevo on Wednesday will be continued on Friday.
- The Croat Democratic Party (HDZ) from Mostar asks the OSCE chief of mission in Bosnia, Robert Frowick, to hold new municipal elections in Mostar at the same time as in the rest of the country.
- Bosnian National bank offers to sell 25 million German marks to commercial banks in Bosnia in return for Bosnian dinars. In two earlier sales, the banks bought 40 million marks.
- A Bosnian opposition leader, Sejfudin Tokic, believes that the infiltration of crime into Bosnia's political structure threatens the country's stability.
